name: 00_Readme
title: Supplemental Digital Content 2: submission results workbook

blocks.label: Scope and interpretation
rows: Current manuscript results and necessary sensitivity analyses only. No new estimates or statistical refits were performed during workbook consolidation.
25 worksheets: this guide; Tables 1 to 3; S01 to S21 matching SDC 1 Tables S1 to S21. Each results sheet starts with the publication table and then provides supporting estimates where needed.
Publication strings retain their displayed precision. Detailed numeric values are copied at source precision. This is a static results workbook, not an interactive statistical model.

Primary: 164 distinct recovery confirmation times in 78 patients, 20 s normal confirmation. Adjustment-pair weighting, patient weighting and 30/60 s definitions are labelled sensitivities. Restricted-mean minutes are a different estimand.
Timing-state estimates and CI limits are fractions, not percentages; multiply by 100 to express percentages. Horizon and normal_sec are seconds; interval_min is minutes.

AUC ratios, event probabilities and unavailable fractions are fractions; contrasts between these are fraction differences. Multiply differences by 100 for percentage points. TWA is mmHg; visible delay is minutes; state discordance is min per hour.

Infusion display-state values and QC columns ending percent are percentages. HDR/ODR and NetBias are fractions. Outcome estimates are relative risks. The publication headers and detailed metric/unit columns govern each block.
lo/hi or lower/upper columns are 95% confidence limits, not patient quantiles. n.a. and reporting-gate failures are retained. Blank CI cells do not mean zero uncertainty.

original_all: full original timing cohort; original_matched_core60 / matched_original: same records before objective-onset masking; core60: after objective-onset masking. original/qc60/qc_all/startup10: original, sustained startup masking, all flagged-bin masking, and exclusion of the first 600 s.

unit_equal / event_equal: equal event or recovery weights after averaging phases; patient_equal: average defined within-patient ratios. Pooled AUC ratios are burden-weighted and pooled event proportions are event-weighted.

Original paired-support estimates retain their original bootstrap CIs. Common-valid-support estimates use the 20261016 paired bootstrap. The duplicate rebootstrap of original support is archived separately.
Original VitalDB cohort: 2435 operations, 2380 patients. Harmonised cohorts and onset-matched timing cohorts differ; use the denominator belonging to the result, not a common denominator.
Aggregate results only. No patient identifiers, individual records or waveform trajectories are included. Algorithmic signal-quality sensitivity analyses are not physician adjudication.

The complete 125-sheet source workbook is retained separately as SDC2_Historical_125_Sheets_20261016.xlsx. Old numbered tables, superseded timing outputs, duplicate display tables and ancillary diagnostic strata are not part of this submission workbook.

Reproducibility release v2.0.1, 16 October 2026. Four S15 integer counts corrected; estimates and confidence intervals unchanged. The version-specific Zenodo DOI is recorded at https://github.com/tqytqytqytqy/ioh-bidirectional-misclassification/releases/tag/v2.0.1.

Current manuscript Tables 1 to 3 and SDC 1 Tables S1 to S21; frozen aggregate results from the 2026-10-16 ethics-and-citation revision. The separate archive contains the exact original workbook and the source-cell selection manifest.

name: Table_1
title: Table 1. Characteristics of the original intraoperative VitalDB cohort
notes: Values are median [interquartile range] or n (% among valid nonmissing cases). ASA Physical Status was missing in 54 cases; percentages use 2381 cases with valid values. Four included non-donor operations carried source-recorded ASA=6 values incompatible with the operative context; because no audit trail was available for adjudication, these values were treated as missing. No ASA V cases were recorded. ASA, American Society of Anesthesiologists; NIBP, noninvasive blood pressure.

name: Table_2
title: Table 2. Harmonized minute-reference technical replication
notes:
Minute reference, events >=180 s
All values refer to MAP below 65 mmHg and a 5 min emulated display, averaged across every grid-compatible phase. Hidden and overdisplay areas are percentages of total reference deficit AUC; net difference is displayed minus reference AUC, divided by reference AUC. Never-low episodes have no displayed low value at any time during the episode. Episodes last at least 180 s. Unavailable display is distinct from normal display.
VitalDB and MIMIC minutes are medians of six 10 s bins with at least five valid bins; SICdb supplies native minutes. Original-grid complete hours require at least 48 valid minutes. Valid reference hours exclude missing bins. These recording sets are distinct from the original 2435-case VitalDB cohort. MIMIC contains 50 eligible patients from the screened set, not the entire public waveform database.
Ratios are pooled from summed components; confidence intervals use 1000 patient-cluster bootstrap replicates. Patients with defined AUC/event ratios number 1783/1329 in VitalDB, 42/41 in MIMIC and 18 170/16 762 in SICdb. Table S14 reports equal-patient estimates. AUC, area under the deficit curve; CI, confidence interval; MAP, mean arterial pressure.

name: Table_3
title: Table 3. Display information at infusion adjustment and after distinct arterial recovery
notes:
A. Display states at recorded infusion adjustment
236 adjustments during MAP <65 mmHg in 85 operations from 83 patients. Entries average all compatible sampling phases and sum to 100% before rounding. These are emulated display states. The original adjustment analysis uses 1/2.5/5 min intervals.
B. Low display persisting after distinct arterial recovery
164 distinct recovery confirmation times in 80 operations from 78 patients, corresponding to 184 adjustment-recovery pairs. Each recovery has equal weight after phase averaging. Recovery requires 20 s of consecutive normal completed bins; follow-up starts at confirmation. Persistence requires both normal reference pressure and low display throughout the horizon. Unknown follow-up remains in the denominator. Timing analyses use 1/3/5 min intervals. CIs use patient-cluster bootstrap resampling. Complete states, recovery-definition sensitivities and objective-onset results appear in Tables S6 to S8. CI, confidence interval; MAP, mean arterial pressure.

blocks.label: Original burden versus completed-bin timing grid

notes: MAP threshold: 65 mmHg. All 2435 cases and 2380 subjects are included. The reference row uses observed arterial pressure and represents all 9187 qualifying reference events. Intermittent rows are averages across all 10 s sampling phases; fractional event counts are expected counts, not additional independent events. An event lasts ≥60 s and has low display if any held value is below threshold, including an inherited value. Duration and AUC cover all below-threshold bins, including runs <60 s, not only qualifying events. Pooled TWA is total deficit AUC / 532 190.5 min of valid reference observation, using the same denominator throughout. Initial unavailable display contributes no displayed burden and is not normal pressure. CI resamples subjects (1000 replicates). Detailed uncertainty is in the complete absolute interval estimates in Supplemental Digital Content 2 (worksheet S03_Exposure); directional decomposition is retained in SDC 2 worksheet S03_Exposure. AUC, area under the deficit curve; CI, confidence interval; MAP, mean arterial pressure; TWA, time-weighted average.

name: S04_Case_Variation
title: Table S4. Case-level variation under a 5 min display
notes: Mean arterial pressure threshold: 65 mmHg. Each case contributes one average across 30 sampling phases. Area ratios require positive reference deficit area; 42 zero-area cases remain in absolute state-discordance summaries. State discordance excludes display-unavailable time. Case summaries are not pooled exposure ratios. Among 1899 cases with ≥60 s episodes, the miss fraction was 36.7% [24.8 to 50.2%], with 5th to 95th percentiles 3.3 to 70.0%; within-case phase range was 66.7 [50.0 to 100.0] percentage points. Aggregate quantiles are in the workbook; case-level trajectories are not redistributed.

notes:
MAP <65 mmHg; 5 min display; 30 phases. Percentage entries are estimates (95% subject-cluster bootstrap CI; 1000 replicates, seed 20260706); no-low-display cells also give reference episode count n. Gap allowance bridges only finite observed normal-pressure bins, never missing reference. Minimum duration counts cumulative low-pressure time, excluding normal gaps. Each definition has a different event population; row counts are not independent cohorts. Fresh and inherited-only entries use the original population. Startup rules preserve original phases and are defined in the startup-quality methods. Longer events are less often missed; these estimates do not describe treatment effects.
In the first 600 s after first finite reference MAP, flag 10 s bins with numeric MAP <40 mmHg, waveform coverage >=80% and p95-p05 <=5 mmHg. Sustained masking requires >=60 s consecutively flagged; all-bin masking has no run-length requirement. Both reapply >=80% whole-window reference coverage. Cases without source waveforms remain. Window exclusion retains the original cohort and can remove true early hypotension. These were algorithmic sensitivity rules.
Affected cases and removed valid-reference time are counted before coverage exclusions. Results use MAP <65 mmHg, a 5 min display and 30 phases; episodes require >=60 s of continuous finite low MAP. Parentheses give 95% subject-cluster percentile CIs (1000 replicates). The final three rows are mutually exclusive and sum to 100% before rounding. Original grids and phases remain; masked values cannot update sampling, and missing reference breaks episodes. AUC, area under the deficit curve; MAP, mean arterial pressure.
